memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "For the unclean person, put some ashes from the burned purification offering into a jar and pour fresh water over them. Then a man who is ceremonially clean is to take some hyssop, dip it in the water and sprinkle the tent and all the furnishings and the people who were there. He must also sprinkle anyone who has touched a human bone or a grave or anyone who has been killed or anyone who has died a natural death." — Num 19:17-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Now we see how the cleansing was applied. The ashes of the heifer were mixed with fresh, running water, and this "water of cleansing" was sprinkled on the unclean person using hyssop. What was defiled by death could be made clean again through this God-given provision. Restoration was possible; uncleanness did not have to be permanent.

Notice the beautiful combination: the ashes of a past sacrifice mixed with fresh, living water. The cleansing drew on something already accomplished — the heifer already offered — applied afresh through water to the one in need. The sacrifice was in the past, but its cleansing power was applied in the present moment of need.

This is a picture of how grace works in our lives. The great sacrifice has already been made, once for all, at the cross. We do not need it repeated. But its cleansing power is applied to us again and again, fresh for every new stain, whenever we come to God in faith. The finished work of Christ meets our present need.

The imagery of water for cleansing runs right through Scripture to Christ. Jesus spoke of living water He would give, and of being cleansed by "the washing with water through the word." His Spirit applies the cleansing His cross accomplished, fresh to us each day. The psalmist prayed, "Cleanse me with hyssop, and I will be clean; wash me, and I will be whiter than snow." That prayer is answered fully in Jesus. What the water of cleansing pictured, Christ provides in truth: a washing that makes us whiter than snow.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does it comfort you that Christ's finished work is applied fresh to your present need?
2. Do you come to God for cleansing whenever you are stained by sin?
3. What does it mean to you to be washed "whiter than snow" in Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that the sacrifice of Christ was made once for all, yet its cleansing is applied fresh to me each day. Wash me and I will be clean; cleanse me and I will be whiter than snow. Thank You for the living water of Your Spirit. Amen.
